title: Warframe
subtitle: Eight always-on mod slots and shields

entries.title: Warframe Arsenal
entries.summary: Where Warframe mods go: recipe and use

blocks.text: The {item:kuvalich:requiem_warframe_table} is where you install <hl>Warframe mods</hl> on yourself. Installed mods are <g>always active</g> - you do not need to hold anything or wear armor.

Here, "Warframe" simply means you, the player. "Mods" are cards that add stats, and they come in two kinds: weapon mods and Warframe mods. For any other unfamiliar term, see the [[start/glossary|Glossary]].

In the original game, a Warframe is a biomechanical combat suit the player controls, each with its own look and abilities. The Arsenal is the station on your ship where you pick Warframes and weapons and install mods.
How to build it

rows: <t>×1</t> <w>the whole block is consumed</w> - [[weapons/requiem_evolve|build another]] if you still need one

blocks.title: Not an early-game build
blocks.text:
A {item:kuvalich:lich_reliquary} drops only when you kill the [[enemies/kuva_master|Kuva Lich]] boss with a successful [[requiem/decryption|decryption]] - that is, you got all three Requiem cards and their order right. <t>1</t> per kill.
The {item:kuvalich:requiem_evolve} (the workbench for upgrading weapons) also takes <t>1</t> in its own recipe, so you need at least two Lich victories.
<dim>Where each material comes from: [[start/materials]].</dim>
How to use it

items: Place it and right-click. The two top rows, <t>8</t> slots in total, are your Warframe mod slots.
Drag a mod into an empty slot, or <t>Shift + left-click</t> it in your inventory to send it to the first slot that accepts it. Only Warframe mods fit here.
A mod <g>takes effect the moment it goes in</g> and stops the moment it comes out - no need to close the screen.
Press <t>Tab</t> to open the Warframe side of the [[modules/module_codex|Mod Codex]].

blocks.text: Mod won't go in?

items: <w>Not revealed yet</w>: a mod whose stats show ??? must be revealed first - hold it in your main hand and right-click. The revealed mod drops at your feet.
<w>Only one mod per family</w>: e.g. Vitality, Vitality Prime and Executioner Vitality are versions of one family, so only one of them can go in.
Mods with unrelated names can share a family too, such as Athena and Redirection.
At most <t>1</t> [[modules/riven_module|Riven mod]] (a mod whose stats are all random) can be installed.
Mods that add <t>loot drop multiplier</t> exclude each other, and so do mods that add <t>ore drop multiplier</t>; Riven mods are exempt from this rule.
While you hold a mod on the cursor, installed mods that conflict with it flash red.

blocks.title: Mods live on you, not in the block
blocks.text: Your eight slots follow you: any Arsenal you open shows your own mods, and other players see theirs. Death, changing dimension and returning from the End all keep them intact - they never drop. Breaking the Arsenal does not touch them either.

blocks.title: Mine it with diamond
blocks.text: You need a diamond pickaxe or better to get the Arsenal back - the wrong tool destroys it with no drop. It is twice as hard as obsidian, so it takes a while.

entries.title: How Warframe Mods Work
entries.summary: Always on, how values stack, when each stat applies

blocks.text: Mods installed in the [[warframe/warframe_table|Warframe Arsenal]] are <g>active at all times</g>: fighting, mining, travelling, even empty-handed, and no armor is required.
How to tell: a Warframe mod's last tooltip line reads "{lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_type.tooltip}"; a weapon mod's reads "{lang:kuvaweapon.item_type.tooltip}". Neither kind fits the other's slots.

items: kuvalich:warframe_common_module
kuvalich:warframe_uncommon_module
kuvalich:warframe_rare_module
kuvalich:warframe_prime_module
kuvalich:warframe_riven_module
blocks.caption: The five Warframe mod tiers (rarities) - see [[modules/module_rarity]]

blocks.text: Where they come from, and spares

items.text: Mining [[world/requiem_ore|Requiem Ore]] and fighting [[enemies/kuva_slave|Kuva Thralls]] and the [[enemies/kuva_master|Kuva Lich]] boss can all drop mods; <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.moduleWeaponRatio|mul:-1|add:100|pctv}</t> of them are Warframe mods, the rest are weapon mods.

Mods from mining [[world/requiem_ore|Requiem Ore]] and from [[enemies/kuva_slave|Kuva Thralls]] and the [[enemies/kuva_master|Kuva Lich]] boss are all weapon mods - Warframe mods never drop from them.
Put three spare Warframe mods into the [[weapons/requiem_recast|Requiem Recast]] to combine them into one.

items: A single Warframe mod placed in the [[weapons/requiem_recast|Requiem Recast]] on its own is broken down into {item:kuvalich:endo}.

blocks.text: In the original game, mods are sorted by what they fit: Warframe mods go only on Warframes, and rifle, shotgun, melee and other weapon mods only on that kind of weapon.
How values stack

items.text: Each mod's real value = its max-rank value × current rank ÷ <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.moduleMaxLevel}</t>. The tooltip already shows the adjusted number; ranking up uses {item:kuvalich:endo} - see [[modules/module_level]].
Mods have no ranks - every mod works at full value.

items: The same stat across your eight mods is simply added up; negative values cancel out positive ones.

Exceptions: {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.fireProtection}, {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.electricProtection}, {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.homologousProtection}, {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.fallProtection} and {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.shieldRecoveryDelay} multiply, and resistance from kill stacks multiplies on top.

blocks.text: 60% {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.fireProtection} on a mod + 50% from stacks → you take 40% × 50% = 20% (not 110% immunity)
Five stats that become vanilla attributes

{lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.health}, {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.armor}, {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.sprintSpeed}, {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.knockbackResistance} and {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.reachDistance} are converted into vanilla attributes, refreshed every <t>0.25</t> s.

blocks.title: Remainders are dropped
blocks.text: These five count in whole <t>10%</t> steps, <w>rounded down</w>: +25% is really +20%, and anything under +10% does nothing. Negative values count in steps too, and {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.health} never goes below -90%.

items: {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.armor} scales the armor and armor toughness you already have - with no armor on and no other armor source, any percentage is still 0.
{lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.sprintSpeed} actually raises movement speed, so walking gets faster too.
{lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.reachDistance} only extends how far you can reach blocks, not your attack reach.

blocks.text: Other stats

{lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.fireProtection}, {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.electricProtection}, {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.homologousProtection}, {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.fallProtection}: when you are hit, they cut the part of that hit that reaches your health by a percentage. "Homologous" means damage from other players.

rows: All healing × (1 + value); at a total of -100% or lower you cannot heal at all
Mining speed × (1 + value); at a total of -100% or lower you cannot break any block

cells: Animals and monsters you kill drop more, at <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.itemDropEffectMultiplier|pctv}</t> effectiveness
Ores you mine drop more - see [[world/ore_drop_multiplier]]

blocks.text: Kill-stack stats
Stats whose name says "Gained on kill" are <hl>kill stacks</hl>: the more you kill, the bigger the bonus, and it fades once you stop killing. Details in [[combat/kill_stack]].

items: Each killing blow you land (melee or ranged) gives every kill-stack stat you have <t>+1</t> stack, up to its own cap - caps are in [[reference/warframe_attr_killstack]].
The bonus = value per stack × current stacks.
After your last kill you lose <t>1</t> stack every <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.warframeStackDecayTicks|sec}</t>; logging out clears them.

blocks.text: Advanced details

items: If the final blow is damage triggered by an [[combat/elements|element]], you gain no Warframe stacks - e.g. burning, Toxin or Slash damage over time, or the extra Electric or Blast damage.

items.text: {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.itemDropMultiplier}: gear and tools with durability are not multiplied; slimes, ghasts, phantoms and the like do not count as monsters and get no bonus.
Consecrated items (items that can hold mods) in the offhand, armor slots and Curios slots lend weapon mods to your main hand - a separate system from Warframe mods; see [[modules/multi_slot]].

items: Limits on mod values apply to Warframe mods too - see [[modules/module_limits]].
Stat-by-stat details: [[reference/warframe_attr_survival]], [[reference/warframe_attr_resist]], [[reference/warframe_attr_mobility]], [[reference/warframe_attr_killstack]].

entries.title: Shields
entries.summary: Yellow-heart shields: cap, recharge, delay, pitfalls

blocks.text: Your <hl>shield</hl> is vanilla's <t>yellow hearts</t> (absorption). When you are hit, armor reduces the damage first, then yellow hearts soak it up, and only what is left hits your health.
As long as your [[warframe/warframe_module|Warframe mods]] give a total {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.shield} above 0, your yellow hearts slowly refill to the cap on their own.

blocks.title: Shield Capacity backfires
blocks.text: {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.shield} gives you no yellow hearts at all. While you have it, yellow hearts from other sources such as golden apples get wiped too - they only last for a while after you get hit or hit something.
Shield cap
Shield cap = max health × {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.shield} × {cfg:kuva_lich.shieldCapMultiplier}
Max health is one of the factors, so stacking {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.health} raises your shield cap as well.
When recharging starts
Shields do not recharge all the time: after you take damage or hit something, there is a wait before they start.

rows: You got hit or hit something, yellow hearts left
Wait <t>10 s</t> × delay factor, then start recharging

items: With no {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.shieldRecoveryRate}, empty to full takes <t>100 s</t>; with +100% it takes <t>50 s</t>.
Delay factor = the product of (1 + {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.shieldRecoveryDelay}) over your mods; negative values shorten the wait.

Kill stacks can feed shields too (see [[combat/kill_stack]]): {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.shield} stacks up to <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.maxStacksShield}</t> times, {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.shieldRecoveryRate} up to <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.maxStacksShieldRecoveryRate}</t>, {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.shieldRecoveryDelay} up to <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.maxStacksShieldRecoveryDelay}</t>.

blocks.title: Hitting things also resets the wait
blocks.text:
Shields barely recharge while you keep fighting and only come back once you stop.
Once your yellow hearts are empty, every hit you take or land restarts the tripled wait (base <t>30 s</t>).
In the original game, Warframe shields also take damage before health and recharge on their own after a short time without being hit; if they are fully depleted, the wait before recharging is longer.
Advanced details

items: Shields block first, resistances apply after: {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.fireProtection} and the like only reduce the part that gets through to your health.

items.text: The wait is rounded down to whole seconds. Mod values carry a tiny extra fraction (a tooltip -30% is really -30.01%), so -30% gives <t>6</t> s, not 7.
While you have {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.shield}, yellow hearts above the cap (e.g. from an enchanted golden apple) are trimmed to the cap whenever you are not in the wait.
After respawning, yellow hearts start from 0. The killing blow has usually already started a tripled wait, which must run out before they recharge; time on the death screen does not count.

items: {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.fixedShield}: none of the built-in mods have it; it only appears on extra custom mods. When present, the cap is exactly that many points instead of being based on {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.shield}.

blocks.text: If whoever hits you holds a consecrated weapon (a weapon that can hold mods) - another player, for example - some elements act differently against yellow hearts. Details in [[combat/element_status]]:

rows: Damage over time goes around them straight to health
Damage over time always hits health directly
Under Magnetic status, you take more damage while you have them
Deals <t>3</t> times as much to a target with them as to one without
Half damage to targets with them

entries.title: Curios Slots
entries.summary: Consecrated trinkets lend weapon mods to your main hand

blocks.text: A consecrated item (an item that can hold mods) worn in a Curios slot can lend the weapon mods on it to your main-hand weapon, at a reduced rate.

blocks.title: Not the same as Warframe mods
blocks.text: Warframe mods only go in the {item:kuvalich:requiem_warframe_table} and never need a Curios slot.
How to set it up

items: Pick an item that can be worn in a Curios slot. This mod adds no trinkets of its own, so use a ring, necklace or similar from another mod.
Put it (a single item) into the {item:kuvalich:requiem_evolve} with a {item:kuvalich:riven_sliver} to <hl>consecrate</hl> it.
Install weapon mods on it in the {item:kuvalich:requiem_weapon_table}.
Wear it. From then on, whenever your main hand holds a consecrated weapon, those stats are added to it using the formula below.

blocks.text: Stat from a trinket = its weapon mods' value × {cfg:kuva_lich.curiosEffectMultiplier|pctv} × the trinket's own {lang:kuvalich.attr.short.damage}

items: Every consecrated item you wear counts, each worked out separately.

items.text: Only the first <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.curiosModuleMaxSlots}</t> Curios slots count; trinkets in later slots do not.

items: The {lang:kuvalich.attr.short.damage} the trinket rolled when consecrated is a factor too: 150% counts as ×1.5, 60% leaves only 60%. Reroll it with a [[weapons/forma|Forma]] if you are unhappy with it.
<w>If your main hand is not a consecrated weapon, trinkets give nothing.</w>
Your main-hand weapon's panel includes the trinket bonuses. <dim>The panel may not match exactly; actual damage is what counts.</dim>

blocks.text: The offhand and armor slots follow the same rules with different rates - see [[modules/multi_slot]].
